corrections.why: NHLR describes a 60 ft Aermotor tower and the plaque says 60-foot-tall. 7.6 m is about 25 ft, which matches the 1936 plan for a 25-foot observation tower on Two Mile Hill rather than the built tower.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: A 1936 Portsmouth Times item describes a planned 25-foot observation tower on Two Mile Hill, open to the public. The NHLR entry and the plaque describe a 60-foot tower built in 1925 and do not mention Two Mile Hill. The sources do not say whether these are the same structure, so the story treats the 1936 plan as unconfirmed.

sources.title: Brush Ridge Fire Tower Historical Marker

notes_for_editor: Height corrected from 7.6 m (likely the 1936 25-foot plan) to 60 ft per NHLR and plaque. Build year 1925 rests on NHLR and the plaque, which agree. Aermotor make comes from NHLR only. 'Still standing' is the plaque plus the undated FLO list, not a current inspection. Access: the forest is public land, but climbing permission is not confirmed. The NHLR bird's-eye GIF exists but was not added as a photo (relative link). Brush Ridge marker [6] used only for statewide context (Ohio's first fire tower, 1922; CCC construction of fire towers, 1933-1935), not for this tower. The story now dates the statewide push to 1922 and 1933-1935 instead of the broader 1920s-1930s range.
